grades.quote: An SC may succeed only if no store from another hart to the reservation set can be observed to have occurred between the LR and the SC, and if there is no other SC between the LR and itself in program order.
grades.reason: Gives the conditions under which an SC can succeed or fail: another hart's store to the reservation set, an intervening SC, or a non-hart device write. It also explains the result code: failure is non-zero, 1 means unspecified failure, and portable software should only assume non-zero. It covers misalignment exceptions too.

grades.quote: executing a CMO instruction may cause a constrained LR/SC loop on any hart to fail periodically
grades.reason: Only auxiliary. It says CMO instructions executed by other harts can cause LR/SC failures, which is one extra cause of failure. It does not explain the basic failure conditions or the SC result value.

grades.quote: the SC.W succeeds only if the reservation is still valid and the reservation set contains the bytes being written
grades.reason: Directly describes SC.W semantics. It succeeds only if the reservation is still valid and covers the written bytes. On success it writes zero to rd, and on failure it writes a nonzero value and does not write memory. Any SC.W also invalidates the hart's reservation.
About NTL hints inside LR/SC loops and forward progress. It says nothing about why SC.W fails or what its result indicates.
